data_schema.title: USDA Directive Extraction Schema v2.1 (DR/DM)
data_schema.description: Extracts metadata and structured policy statements from 3000 series USDA Departmental Regulation (DR) or Departmental Manual (DM). Governing rules: (1) Any field described as verbatim must be copied character-for-character from the source document. Never paraphrase, merge, abbreviate, summarize, or insert ellipses. (2) Do not infer. If the source does not support an optional field, leave the field out entirely. Never return an empty string or a guess. (3) Only the label fields in policy_statements (statement_kind, statement_function, modal_use, normative_force, actor_basis) are interpretations. Every other field is quoted or copied from the document.

document_type.description: Type of document as printed in the header, such as 'Departmental Regulation' or 'Departmental Manual'.

issuing_organization.description: Organization issuing the document, verbatim from the header.

issuing_location.description: Location of the issuing organization, verbatim from the header.

regulation_number.description: Official document number from the header, verbatim, for example 'DR 3105-001'.

subject.description: Subject or title of the document, verbatim from the header.

issue_date.description: Issue date from the header, as written.

expiration_date.description: Expiration date from the header, as written. Leave out if none is printed.

opi.description: Office of Primary Interest (OPI) from the header, verbatim.

supersedes.description: The prior document this document supersedes. Take all values from the supersession paragraph in the body (usually under Special Instructions/Cancellations), NOT from the header. Leave the whole object out if the document supersedes nothing.

document_number.description: Number of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph. If it is identical to this document's own number, still copy it from the supersession paragraph, not the header.

document_title.description: Title of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

document_date.description: Date of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

scope.description: The text of the Scope section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Scope section.

purpose.description: The text of the Purpose section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Purpose section.

inquiries.description: Contact information from the Inquiries section. Leave out any property the document does not state; never return an empty string.

office.description: Office or division named for inquiries, verbatim. Leave out if the document names no office.

email.description: Email address given for inquiries, verbatim, without trailing punctuation. Leave out if none is given.

table_of_contents.description: Top-level entries of the printed table of contents, in order, including appendices. Return an empty list if the document prints no table of contents.

section_number.description: Section or appendix identifier as printed, for example '1.' or 'Appendix A'.

section_title.description: Section or appendix title as printed in the table of contents.

page.description: Page number exactly as printed in the table of contents, for example '2' or 'A-1'. Copy it even if the section actually starts on a different page. Leave out if no page number is printed.

actors.description: Registry of every distinct entity that the policy text names in an acting role. One entry per entity. Include every entity used as actor_name in policy_statements. Also include entities the document names in a role without being directed to act (mark those mentioned_only). Documents (bylaws, regulations, directives) are NEVER actors and must not appear here. Return an empty list if the document names no actors.

name.description: The entity's name exactly as written in the policy text, without a leading article ('the') and without a possessive. Keep a compound name intact if the document writes it as one phrase, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'. This is the join key used by actor_name in policy_statements, so spell it identically there.

components.description: ONLY for a name that joins separate entities with commas or 'and' (for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices' gives 'USDA Mission Areas', 'agencies', 'staff offices'). NEVER split a job title from the organization that qualifies it ('Director of IT, Office of the Inspector General' is ONE position), and never split an organization name from the position it modifies ('Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) Associate CIOs (ACIO)' is ONE group). Each component is a verbatim substring of the name. Leave out for single entities.

items.description: One verbatim component of a compound actor name.

actor_type.description: Kind of entity. Use exactly one of: position (a job title, singular or plural, for example 'USDA CIO' or 'Mission Area Assistant CIOs'), office (an organizational unit, for example 'OCIO Executive Secretariat'), council_or_body (a council, committee, board, or similar body), group (a category of organizations or units, not job titles, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'), external_entity (an entity outside the document's authority), program_or_system (an IT initiative, system, program, or project that the document says must act or conform).

binding_status.description: bound_by_this_document: the document directs, permits, or assigns a function or role to this entity and has authority over it. mentioned_only: the document names the entity but cannot or does not impose anything on it (for example a council or agency outside USDA that the document says a USDA body partners with).

policy_statements.description: Structured statements from the numbered body sections only (not the table of contents, not the appendices). RULES. (a) SENTENCES: emit one statement per sentence. If a paragraph has more than one sentence, give each its own statement with ids suffixed .s1, .s2, and so on. Abbreviations and legal citations ('U.S.C.', 'CFR', '§', 'et seq.') do not end a sentence. (b) LISTS: when text introduces a list (usually ends with a colon, for example 'The USDA CIO will:'), emit the introducing text as one statement with statement_kind 'lead_in', and emit EVERY item of the list as its own statement with statement_kind 'list_item' and parent_statement_id set to the id of the lead_in. Never skip list items, including lists of legal authorities. For a list inside a list, parent_statement_id is the immediate parent. (c) NEVER merge text from different sentences, paragraphs, or list items into one statement. (d) Copy text exactly; do not summarize. (e) PRONOUNS: when a sentence's subject is a pronoun ('It', 'Its', 'They') that refers to a named actor in the preceding sentence, resolve it: set actor_name to that actor and actor_basis to resolved_from_prior_sentence. (f) DOCUMENT AS SUBJECT: when the grammatical subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'), leave actor_name out; the entities the document acts on belong in target.

statement_id.description: Printed numbering path of the statement: section number, then paragraph letter, then item number in parentheses, for example '1', '3.a', '5.d.s2', '6.a(1)'. Add '.sN' only when a paragraph contains more than one sentence. Must be unique within the document.

statement_kind.description: standalone: a complete sentence that stands on its own. lead_in: text that introduces a list and is incomplete without its items. list_item: a list item that completes its lead_in.

parent_statement_id.description: Include ONLY when statement_kind is list_item: the statement_id of its immediate lead_in. For every other statement leave this field out entirely; never return an empty string.

section_number.description: Number of the section containing the statement, digits only, for example '6'.

section_title.description: Title of the section containing the statement, as shown in the table of contents, for example 'Roles and Responsibilities'.

source_text.description: VERBATIM text of this one sentence or list item exactly as printed, including trailing punctuation such as ':' or ';' and including any list-ending words such as 'and'. No paraphrase, no ellipses, no text from any other statement. For a list_item, give only the item's own text, not the lead_in.

statement_function.description: What the statement does. obligation: a required action or compliance requirement on an actor. responsibility: a standing duty or function assigned to an actor, including present-tense descriptions of what a body does. role_designation: assigns an entity to a role, for example membership or voting status. authority: names a legal source of authority or a grant of authority. scope: states what or whom the document applies to. purpose: states why the document or a body exists. definition: defines a term. condition: states a standalone triggering condition. exception: carves out an exception. savings_clause: states that the document does not displace existing authorities or delegations. effectivity: states when the document takes effect or how long it lasts. supersession: states that the document replaces another. classification_rule: states a rule that classifies something or applies a requirement when a status is met. reference: points to another document or location. inquiry: tells who may be contacted. container: use for every lead_in statement. other: none of the above.

modal_verb.description: The modal word or phrase of the statement's MAIN clause, exactly as written, for example 'will', 'can', 'may', 'must', 'shall', 'must not'. Ignore modals inside relative or subordinate clauses (for 'advises the USDA CIO on IT matters that may become IT investments', the 'may' is not the statement's modal). For a list_item whose own text has no modal, copy the modal from its lead_in. Leave out if the main clause has no modal.

modal_use.description: deontic: the main-clause modal directs, permits, or prohibits action by an actor (for example 'The Deputy CIO will serve', 'can direct questions'). predictive: the modal only states what will happen or remain true (for example 'It will remain in effect until superseded'). none: the main clause has no modal.

normative_force.description: mandatory: deontic 'will', 'shall', or 'must' directing an actor to act or to serve in a role. prohibitive: deontic 'must not', 'shall not', or 'may not'. permissive: deontic 'may' or 'can'. assigned: a present-tense statement with no deontic modal that assigns or describes a function, duty, or role of a named actor (for example 'The CIO Council advises the USDA CIO on...', 'It assesses the needs of...'); use it only when actor_name is present, and never for purpose statements. descriptive: everything else with no deontic force, including purpose, scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, references, authorities, definitions, and statements about the document itself or about other documents. not_applicable: use for every lead_in; its force is carried by its list_items.

actor_name.description: The entity directed to act, permitted to act, or assigned a function or role by this statement, spelled exactly as in the matching actors[].name. It must appear in source_text or in the lead_in's text (leading article removed); for a resolved pronoun, copy it from the antecedent sentence. Leave out when the statement binds no actor: scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, statements about documents (including bylaws), and any statement whose subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'). Never supply an actor that is not stated in the text or resolvable from the preceding sentence. Always leave out for lead_in statements.

actor_basis.description: Include ONLY when actor_name is present; otherwise leave this field out entirely. explicit_in_statement: the actor appears in this statement's own source_text. inherited_from_lead_in: the actor appears only in the lead_in that this list_item completes. resolved_from_prior_sentence: the subject is a pronoun resolved to the actor named in the preceding sentence.

target.description: VERBATIM phrase naming what the action is directed at or what the statement applies to, starting at the first word after any leading article ('a', 'an', 'the'). For a role_designation, the body or unit the role is within (for example 'CIO Council'). Leave out if none.

resulting_status.description: VERBATIM phrase naming the status or role that a role_designation or classification_rule confers, for example 'voting member' or 'advisory (non-voting) members'. Leave out for other statements.

conditions.description: VERBATIM phrases that restrict when or to what the statement applies, for example 'that the CIO Council designates as enterprise initiatives'. Do NOT treat a non-restrictive descriptive phrase set off by commas (for example 'appointed by the USDA CIO' in 'The Secretariat, appointed by the USDA CIO, will serve') as a condition. Leave out if there are none.

items.description: One verbatim condition phrase copied from source_text.

cross_references.description: Other documents, laws, or regulations cited in source_text, each copied verbatim as ONE entry per cited authority, including its code citation (for example 'The Clinger-Cohen Act of 1996, 40 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 11101 et seq.' is one entry; for a list_item that is just a citation, the entry is the item text without the trailing ';' or 'and'). Never add a separate entry for a title that is part of the same citation (the words 'Chief Information Officer' after '7 CFR § 2.32'). Never list generic categories such as 'law' or 'Federal regulation'. Leave out if none.

acronyms.description: Acronyms and abbreviations listed in the acronym appendix, one entry per row, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no acronym appendix.

acronym.description: Acronym or abbreviation exactly as printed.

authorities_and_references.description: Entries of the Authorities and References appendix, one per entry, each copied verbatim, including any date, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no such appendix.

items.description: One appendix entry exactly as printed, joined across line breaks.

extract_result.subject: Secure Domain Name System
extract_result.opi: Office of the Chief Information Officer, Enterprise Network Services
extract_result.purpose: This Departmental Regulation (DR) establishes the minimum requirements for implementing Domain Name System (DNS) and Domain Name System Security Extensions (DNSSEC) services across all United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) networks.

actors.name: USDA Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO), Enterprise Network Services (ENS) Directorate
agency or staff office Chief Information Officers (CIOs)
ENS or agency technical point of contact (POC) or administrative POC
USDA agencies, staff offices, employees, and contractors

policy_statements.source_text: This Departmental Regulation (DR) establishes the minimum requirements for implementing Domain Name System (DNS) and Domain Name System Security Extensions (DNSSEC) services across all United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) networks.
policy_statements.target: minimum requirements for implementing Domain Name System (DNS) and Domain Name System Security Extensions (DNSSEC) services across all United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) networks

policy_statements.source_text: This DR applies to USDA agencies, staff offices, employees, and contractors responsible for operating and managing DNS equipment and services.
policy_statements.target: USDA agencies, staff offices, employees, and contractors responsible for operating and managing DNS equipment and services

policy_statements.source_text: For any DNS standards not addressed in this policy, refer to the following guidance documents for additional direction and information:
conditions: For any DNS standards not addressed in this policy

policy_statements.source_text: Domain Name System (DNS) Security Reference Architecture, Version 1.0;
cross_references: Domain Name System (DNS) Security Reference Architecture, Version 1.0

policy_statements.source_text: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Special Publication (SP) 800-81-2, Secure Domain Name System (DNS) Deployment Guide;
cross_references: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Special Publication (SP) 800-81-2, Secure Domain Name System (DNS) Deployment Guide

policy_statements.source_text: NIST SP 800-57 Revision 1, Recommendation for Key Management, Part 3: Application-Specific Key Management Guidance;
cross_references: NIST SP 800-57 Revision 1, Recommendation for Key Management, Part 3: Application-Specific Key Management Guidance

policy_statements.source_text: Federal Information Processing Standards (FIPS) Publication (PUB) 140-2, Security Requirements for Cryptographic Modules; and
cross_references: Federal Information Processing Standards (FIPS) Publication (PUB) 140-2, Security Requirements for Cryptographic Modules

policy_statements.source_text: FIPS PUB 186-4, Digital Signature Standard (DSS).
cross_references: FIPS PUB 186-4, Digital Signature Standard (DSS)

policy_statements.source_text: This policy complies with the statutory responsibilities identified in the Federal Information Security Modernization Act of 2014 (FISMA), 44 U.S.C. § 3541, et seq.
cross_references: Federal Information Security Modernization Act of 2014 (FISMA), 44 U.S.C. § 3541, et seq

policy_statements.source_text: This policy adheres to the requirements established in the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Circular A-130, Appendix III, Security of Federal Automated Information Resources and Appendix IV, Analysis of Key Sections.
cross_references: Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Circular A-130, Appendix III, Security of Federal Automated Information Resources
Appendix IV, Analysis of Key Sections

policy_statements.source_text: The following guidance applies to all DNS servers, including USDA enterprise DNS servers and agency and staff office administered DNS servers:

DNS servers shall meet all criteria defined in this policy and must be registered with the USDA Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO), Enterprise Network Services (ENS) Directorate and the Agriculture Security Operations Center (ASOC) in order to operate as a public facing name server.
policy_statements.target: all criteria defined in this policy
conditions: in order to operate as a public facing name server

policy_statements.source_text: The DNS roles of authoritative name server and recursive caching name server shall be separate.
policy_statements.target: DNS roles of authoritative name server and recursive caching name server

policy_statements.source_text: If these roles cannot be separate, an additional statement describing the configuration must be included with the information submitted for registration and USDA Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) authorization.
conditions: If these roles cannot be separate

policy_statements.source_text: In order to comply with OMB, Department of Homeland Security (DHS), and NIST guidance, the USDA enterprise DNS solution shall:
Conform with DHS’s Trusted Internet Connections Reference Architecture Document, Version 2.0 for DNS solutions;
cross_references: Trusted Internet Connections Reference Architecture Document, Version 2.0

policy_statements.source_text: Provide a DNS service that can be offered to USDA agencies and staff offices; and
Comply with relevant NIST, OMB, FIPS, and DHS standards, guidelines, and other processes and controls identified in this policy.
ENS shall implement, operate, and manage the USDA enterprise DNS solution.
This solution shall fully interoperate (without errors) with the Trusted Internet Connections (TICs) and the USDA enterprise network.
policy_statements.target: Trusted Internet Connections (TICs) and the USDA enterprise network

policy_statements.source_text: Public facing authoritative name servers shall:
Prohibit recursive queries from external clients;

Implement DNSSEC signatures for authentication of zone data as mandated in OMB Memorandum M-08-23, Securing the Federal Government’s Domain Name System Infrastructure, and in accordance with NIST SP 800-81-2 and NIST SP 800-57 Revision 1 for zones classified as external in the context of NIST SP 800-53 Revision 4, Security and Privacy Controls for Federal Information Systems and Organizations;
policy_statements.target: DNSSEC signatures for authentication of zone data
conditions: for zones classified as external in the context of NIST SP 800-53 Revision 4, Security and Privacy Controls for Federal Information Systems and Organizations
cross_references: OMB Memorandum M-08-23, Securing the Federal Government’s Domain Name System Infrastructure
NIST SP 800-81-2
NIST SP 800-57 Revision 1
NIST SP 800-53 Revision 4, Security and Privacy Controls for Federal Information Systems and Organizations

policy_statements.source_text: Provide DNS services via both Internet Protocol version 4 (IPv4) and Internet Protocol version 6 (IPv6);
Log queries, access attempts, and provide appropriate audit information to ASOC Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) devices, as directed by the USDA CISO.

These logs shall be transmitted using the system log (syslog) protocol, and as official records, be managed in accordance with Information Technology and Operations Management (ITOM)-11, ITOM-13, and ITOM-23 of the United States Department of Agriculture Record Group 16 File Plan;
cross_references: Information Technology and Operations Management (ITOM)-11, ITOM-13, and ITOM-23 of the United States Department of Agriculture Record Group 16 File Plan

policy_statements.source_text: Secure any zone data transferred between name servers using a secure method such as Transaction Signatures (TSIG), as discussed in NIST SP 800-81-2, or methods providing an equivalent or greater level of data security;
policy_statements.target: any zone data transferred between name servers
cross_references: NIST SP 800-81-2

policy_statements.source_text: Use appropriate address match lists for split DNS views, if defined, to properly segment queries and zone definitions by relevant security contexts;
policy_statements.target: appropriate address match lists for split DNS views
conditions: if defined

policy_statements.source_text: Be configured using the NIST SP 800-81-2 recommended configuration checklist as a guideline; and
cross_references: NIST SP 800-81-2

policy_statements.source_text: Be registered with ENS and ASOC as an authorized USDA public facing authoritative server.
Public facing recursive caching servers shall:
Restrict recursive queries to internal clients only;
Attempt DNSSEC validation for all queried names;
Provide DNS services via both IPv4 and IPv6;
Log queries, access attempts, and provide appropriate audit information to ASOC SIEM devices, as directed by the USDA CISO.
The logs should be transmitted in syslog format and be retained by the owner of the system for a minimum of 30 days;
Provide DNS filtering or security controls such as DNS blackholing, DNS blacklisting, DNS firewall services, or other controls as deemed appropriate by the USDA CISO;
Be configured using the NIST SP 800-81-2 recommended configuration checklist as a guideline;
cross_references: NIST SP 800-81-2

policy_statements.source_text: Be registered with ENS and ASOC as authorized USDA public facing recursive caching resolvers; and
Not host authoritative zones, except for the following:

Locally hosted zones as recommended in the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF) Locally Served DNS Zones, or when necessary to achieve the goals or objectives defined in the IETF Special-Use Domain Names;
conditions: when necessary to achieve the goals or objectives defined in the IETF Special-Use Domain Names
cross_references: Locally Served DNS Zones
Special-Use Domain Names

policy_statements.source_text: Zones hosted in a split view configuration if required by multiple security contexts; and
conditions: if required by multiple security contexts

policy_statements.source_text: Zones necessary to implement a security control as required in section 3d(5).
Internal or private servers shall:
Restrict access to internal queries only;
Forward all unresolvable queries to an authorized public facing recursive caching resolver or to an enterprise internal authoritative server;
Attempt DNSSEC validation for external names and for internal names where appropriate;
conditions: where appropriate

policy_statements.source_text: Provide DNS services on both IPv4 and IPv6 where possible, as directed by OMB mandates and other USDA directives;
conditions: where possible

policy_statements.source_text: Electronically log queries to create an audit trail between the original client query and the resolved DNS response, as directed by the agency or staff office Chief Information Officers (CIOs) or the USDA CISO; and
Be configured using the NIST SP 800-81-2 recommended configuration checklist as a guideline.
cross_references: NIST SP 800-81-2

policy_statements.source_text: DNS services provided to USDA by external, commercial, or other non-USDA sources shall meet the requirements of this policy.

External servers hosting public facing USDA zones must be approved by the USDA CISO as authorized USDA public facing servers and must be included on the authorized USDA DNS server list maintained by ENS.
policy_statements.target: External servers hosting public facing USDA zones

policy_statements.source_text: DNS domains or zones that are external or public facing only shall be hosted on DNS servers that are policy compliant and are authorized USDA public facing servers that meet the requirements identified in section 3c.
policy_statements.target: DNS domains or zones that are external or public facing only

policy_statements.source_text: In order to ensure that the requirements of policy statements defined in section 3 are met, the following internal controls shall be used:
The ENS Director shall review the weekly DHS National Cybersecurity Assessment and Technical Services (NCATS) report detailing issues found with USDA second level non-DNSSEC compliant domains.
policy_statements.target: weekly DHS National Cybersecurity Assessment and Technical Services (NCATS) report

policy_statements.source_text: Upon determining that a DNS domain is noncompliant through a review of the weekly NCATS report or by other means, ENS shall correct all subdomains hosted on the enterprise DNS.
policy_statements.target: all subdomains hosted on the enterprise DNS
conditions: Upon determining that a DNS domain is noncompliant through a review of the weekly NCATS report or by other means

policy_statements.source_text: Agencies and staff offices shall correct any noncompliant domains that they host.
policy_statements.target: any noncompliant domains that they host
conditions: that they host

policy_statements.source_text: ENS shall advise and assist agencies and staff offices in correcting their noncompliant domains.

Agency or staff office domains that remain noncompliant after 45 days following notification shall require the domain owner to either move the domain to a server where it can become DNSSEC compliant, or pursue steps in section 6 to obtain a temporary policy exception waiver until the issue can be corrected.
conditions: that remain noncompliant after 45 days following notification

policy_statements.source_text: The ENS Director shall compile and maintain a list of DNS servers that are authorized by the USDA CISO as policy compliant USDA public facing DNS servers.

The data collected to populate the DNS server list not only serves as an indicator of the level of compliance, but also provides valuable operational data for interactions between the enterprise DNS servers and other authorized DNS servers.

In order to ensure continued validity of the authorized server list, the ENS Director shall coordinate, quarterly, with the ENS or agency technical point of contact (POC) or administrative POC, as appropriate, to verify the information is correct for a random sample of servers from the list.
conditions: quarterly
as appropriate

policy_statements.source_text: ASOC shall continuously monitor inbound and outbound DNS traffic at the USDA network perimeter and identify servers that are sending or receiving DNS queries or answers to or from external destinations.

At the discretion of the USDA CISO, DNS servers not present on the authorized public facing server list may be blocked at the USDA perimeter firewall and be prevented from sending or receiving DNS messages.
policy_statements.target: DNS servers not present on the authorized public facing server list
conditions: At the discretion of the USDA CISO
not present on the authorized public facing server list

policy_statements.source_text: Section 3g specifies that all public facing or “external” zones be hosted on an authorized public facing server.
All public facing zones or subdomains delegated from the enterprise USDA DNS servers to another DNS server shall be hosted on an authorized USDA public facing server.

The ENS Director shall validate annually or at the Key Signing Key (KSK) update interval, whichever is more frequent, that public facing subdomains are delegated to servers that are on the authorized USDA public facing server list.
conditions: annually or at the Key Signing Key (KSK) update interval, whichever is more frequent

policy_statements.source_text: Zones delegated to servers not present on the authorized USDA public facing server list shall either be moved to an authorized server or agencies shall pursue steps identified in section 6 to obtain a temporary policy exception waiver until the identified issue can be corrected.
conditions: delegated to servers not present on the authorized USDA public facing server list

policy_statements.source_text: The ENS Director and USDA CISO may implement additional monitoring tools or controls, or conduct network access tests, to further validate compliance with elements in this policy.
Continued failure to meet the requirements of this policy may result in affected servers being removed from the authorized server list or loss of access through the USDA perimeter firewall.
The USDA CIO shall provide oversight to promote and ensure agency and staff office compliance with this policy.
policy_statements.target: agency and staff office compliance with this policy

policy_statements.source_text: The USDA CISO shall:
Issue access control policy for data and system access, and ensure compliance through assessment and authorization concurrency reviews;
policy_statements.target: access control policy for data and system access

policy_statements.source_text: Define audit log and security control specifications as referenced in sections 3c(4), 3d(4), 3d(5), and 3e(5), and coordinate such guidance with agency and staff offices;
policy_statements.target: audit log and security control specifications

policy_statements.source_text: Enforce DNS policy for the USDA through the use of compliance reviews, automated tools, or other appropriate methodologies;
Review and respond to requests for waivers to this policy;
policy_statements.target: requests for waivers to this policy

policy_statements.source_text: Authorize use of USDA public facing name servers; and
Determine whether DNS servers not on the authorized server list shall be allowed through the USDA perimeter firewall.
The ENS Director shall:
Provide oversight for the implementation and operation of the USDA enterprise DNS;
policy_statements.target: implementation and operation of the USDA enterprise DNS

policy_statements.source_text: Work with agencies and staff offices to provide support, guidance, and delegated DNS services on the enterprise platform;
Develop and provide a DNS service to and for the agencies and staff offices in order to facilitate consolidation of agency and staff office DNS services on the enterprise DNS;
Compile and maintain a current list of authorized public facing name servers.
policy_statements.target: current list of authorized public facing name servers

policy_statements.source_text: This list shall be reviewed and updated quarterly or at DNSSEC KSK rollover periods, whichever is more frequent;
conditions: quarterly or at DNSSEC KSK rollover periods, whichever is more frequent

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure any DNS server hosting a public facing zone delegated from the USDA enterprise DNS is a public facing server authorized by the USDA CISO;
Review the weekly DHS NCATS report, which details issues found with USDA second level non-DNSSEC compliant domains;
Issue guidance for DNS access control and configuration;
policy_statements.target: guidance for DNS access control and configuration

policy_statements.source_text: Provide technical assistance and support on DNS and DNSSEC configurations to the agency or staff office POC implementing this policy;
policy_statements.target: agency or staff office POC implementing this policy

policy_statements.source_text: Maintain a current copy of the DNS authorized server list; and
policy_statements.target: current copy of the DNS authorized server list

policy_statements.source_text: Maintain all necessary documentation provided by agency and staff offices for public facing server registration.
policy_statements.target: all necessary documentation provided by agency and staff offices for public facing server registration

policy_statements.source_text: Agency and Staff Office CIOs shall:
Implement, comply with, and maintain this policy within their respective agency or staff office; and
Provide all necessary documentation to the ENS Director and USDA CISO for public facing server registration.
All USDA agencies and staff offices are required to conform to this policy.
In the event that a policy requirement cannot be met as explicitly stated, the agency or staff office CIO must submit a waiver request to the USDA CISO.
conditions: In the event that a policy requirement cannot be met as explicitly stated

policy_statements.source_text: The waiver request shall explain the reason for the request, identify compensating controls/actions that meet the intent of the policy, and identify how the compensating controls/actions provide a comparable or greater level of defense or compliance than required by the policy.
Agency and staff office CIOs will submit all policy waiver requests to the USDA CISO for review and decision.

Approved waivers from the USDA CISO must be associated with a NIST control that is recorded and tracked as a Plan of Action and Milestones (POA&M) item in the USDA’s FISMA data management and reporting tool.
Waivers will expire at the end of the fiscal year or six months from the date of approval, whichever is longer.
conditions: at the end of the fiscal year or six months from the date of approval, whichever is longer

policy_statements.source_text: Unless otherwise specified, agencies and staff offices shall review and renew approved policy waivers every fiscal year.
conditions: Unless otherwise specified
every fiscal year

policy_statements.source_text: Questions and comments concerning the requirements of this regulation should be directed to OCIO-ENS, Telecommunications Management & Governance (TMG) at <ens.policy@ocio.usda.gov>.

In order to ensure that the requirements of policy statements defined in section 3 are met, the following internal controls shall be used:
The ENS Director shall review the weekly DHS National Cybersecurity Assessment and Technical Services (NCATS) report detailing issues found with USDA second level non-DNSSEC compliant domains.

Upon determining that a DNS domain is noncompliant through a review of the weekly NCATS report or by other means, ENS shall correct all subdomains hosted on the enterprise DNS.

Agencies and staff offices shall correct any noncompliant domains that they host.

ENS shall advise and assist agencies and staff offices in correcting their noncompliant domains.

Agency or staff office domains that remain noncompliant after 45 days following notification shall require the domain owner to either move the domain to a server where it can become DNSSEC compliant, or pursue steps in section 6 to obtain a temporary policy exception waiver until the issue can be corrected.
that remain noncompliant after 45 days following notification
The ENS Director shall compile and maintain a list of DNS servers that are authorized by the USDA CISO as policy compliant USDA public facing DNS servers.

The data collected to populate the DNS server list not only serves as an indicator of the level of compliance, but also provides valuable operational data for interactions between the enterprise DNS servers and other authorized DNS servers.

In order to ensure continued validity of the authorized server list, the ENS Director shall coordinate, quarterly, with the ENS or agency technical point of contact (POC) or administrative POC, as appropriate, to verify the information is correct for a random sample of servers from the list.

ASOC shall continuously monitor inbound and outbound DNS traffic at the USDA network perimeter and identify servers that are sending or receiving DNS queries or answers to or from external destinations.

At the discretion of the USDA CISO, DNS servers not present on the authorized public facing server list may be blocked at the USDA perimeter firewall and be prevented from sending or receiving DNS messages.

All public facing zones or subdomains delegated from the enterprise USDA DNS servers to another DNS server shall be hosted on an authorized USDA public facing server.

The waiver request shall explain the reason for the request, identify compensating controls/actions that meet the intent of the policy, and identify how the compensating controls/actions provide a comparable or greater level of defense or compliance than required by the policy.
